Ran the public suite against the reference (6/6 passed), the sealed suite against the reference (25/25 passed), and the nested-interpreter example (printed 42).
Ran the public suite against the starter and reproduced its documented intentional result (0/6 passed; runner exit 1).
Ran reviewer-authored semantic, diagnostic-line, CLI, exact-capacity, one-over-capacity, and deep-nesting probes under bounded subprocess control.
Inspected both Python runners for argv use, timeout behavior, output capture, and process-tree containment.
Checked the candidate for special files, common credential/private-key patterns, and placement of solution-bearing material.

evidence: GCC 8.5.0 compiled both targets with -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror; supplied Makefile commands reproduced successfully outside immutable CANDIDATE/.
The reference produced the declared 6/6 public passes, 25/25 sealed passes, and output 42 for sealed/reference/examples/meta_vm.mc.
An independent semantic matrix produced exactly 0,0,1,2,3,0,1,-2,-1,-2,1,0,1 on separate lines, and a line-3 division fault exited 70 with a line-3 diagnostic.

Exact advertised capacities succeeded for 1,048,576 source bytes, 65,536 bytecode instructions, 128 functions, 32 parameters, 256 locals, 63-byte identifiers, 8,192 operand values, and 256 active frames; tested one-over cases were diagnosed.

A valid 65,550-byte program containing 32,760 nested parenthesis pairs, 65,534 language tokens and 65,535 stored tokens including EOF terminated by signal 11 with no diagnostic in three of three focused runs.
A valid source containing 65,536 language tokens exited 65 with 'too many tokens'; 65,535 language tokens succeeded because the fixed 65,536-slot table also stores EOF.
The starter accepted '+1' and a leading-space value for --max-steps, while the reference rejected both with usage exit 64.
Both candidate runners use subprocess.run with timeout and captured pipes but do not create or terminate a process group and impose no captured-output bound.
All reference code, sealed tests, production notes, and exercise answers are structurally below sealed/; the only learner-visible C files are the incomplete starter sources.
Manifest status is GENERATED with labels GENERATED and PARTIAL, independent validation REQUIRED, and productionized false; prose consistently disclaims stronger labels.

Project/source/commit/snapshot identifiers are internally consistent, no special files or common credential signatures were found, and the 64-file candidate content digest was 4712c2025215c4db62fb3e08ade721d54e11078fb152ae852c315032c8b2e7b0.
limitations: clang is unavailable, so no second-compiler or cross-platform check was run.
AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer executables could not be linked because their runtime libraries are unavailable.
No fuzz campaign, benchmark, model check, production assessment, or transfer verification was performed; no such label is awarded.
The upstream linked resource was not accessed, so the non-copy assertion, upstream license status, and source snapshot cannot be independently verified from this workspace.
Only the submitted directory structure was inspectable; whether an external learner-view exporter actually excludes sealed/ is inconclusive.
The requirements do not explicitly state whether the synthetic EOF marker counts toward the advertised 65,536-token capacity.
Passing finite suites and reviewer probes do not establish exhaustive language or security correctness.
